entities.name: Nikephoros II Orsini
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nikephoros II Orsini Doukas, a scion of the powerful Italian Orsini family, was the last Latin ruler of the Despotate of Epirus, reigning from 1335 to 1338 and again from 1356 until his death in 1359. His tumultuous rule marked a pivotal period of fragmentation and external interference in the western Balkans, as the region became a battleground between a resurgent Byzantine Empire, an expanding Serbian Empire under Stefan Dušan, and local Albanian lordships. Nikephoros’s attempts to consolidate power and restore the Despotate’s former glory were ultimately thwarted by these competing forces, illustrating the complex geopolitical landscape of the late Byzantine era.

Born to John II Orsini, Despot of Epirus, and Anna Palaiologina, a Byzantine princess, Nikephoros II inherited a precarious throne at the age of seven following his father's assassination in 1335. His mother initially served as regent, but the Byzantine Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos swiftly exploited the instability to reassert imperial control, absorbing Epirus into the Byzantine Empire by 1338. Nikephoros was sent to Constantinople, where he was granted the title of *sebastokrator* and married Maria Kantakouzene, daughter of Emperor John VI Kantakouzene, a strategic alliance intended to integrate him into the Byzantine aristocracy. However, following the collapse of the Serbian Empire after Stefan Dušan's death in 1355, Nikephoros seized the opportunity to return to Epirus in 1356, reclaiming Arta and Ioannina and briefly re-establishing the Despotate.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Nikephoros II Orsini's turbulent reign and death marked the definitive end of the Orsini dynasty's rule in Epirus, directly leading to the fragmentation of the region into smaller Albanian and Serbian lordships and contributing to the eventual Ottoman expansion into the Balkans.
